points.title: 德意志公主
points.description: 叶卡捷琳娜原名索菲娅·奥古斯特·弗里德里卡，出生于普鲁士什切青的一个德意志小公爵家庭。她接受了良好的教育，精通法语、德语等多种语言，阅读了大量哲学和历史著作，特别是启蒙思想家的作品。这段时期的教育为她后来的统治奠定了思想基础，培养了她的政治智慧和文学才能。她通过阅读伏尔泰、孟德斯鸠等启蒙思想家的著作，形成了自己的政治理念。
points.descriptionEn: Born as Sophie Augusta Fredericka in Stettin (now Szczecin, Poland) to a minor German prince, Catherine received an excellent education, mastering multiple languages and extensively reading philosophical and historical works, particularly those of Enlightenment thinkers. This formative period shaped her political wisdom and literary talents. Through her readings of Voltaire, Montesquieu, and other Enlightenment philosophers, she developed her own political philosophy that would later influence her reign.

points.title: 俄国皇储妃
points.description: 1744年，叶卡捷琳娜被选为俄国皇储彼得·乌尔里希（后来的彼得三世）的妻子，来到俄国并皈依东正教，改名为叶卡捷琳娜·阿列克谢耶芙娜。在俄国宫廷中，她面临孤立和排挤，与丈夫关系冷淡。她积极学习俄语，结交朝中大臣，建立自己的政治网络。在此期间，她秘密阅读大量政治书籍，并与伏尔泰等启蒙思想家保持通信。1762年，彼得三世即位后，她发动宫廷政变，推翻丈夫，自立为女皇叶卡捷琳娜二世。
points.descriptionEn: In 1744, Catherine was selected as the wife of the Russian heir Peter Ulrich (later Peter III) and arrived in Russia, converting to Orthodox Christianity and taking the name Catherine Alexeyevna. In the Russian court, she faced isolation and exclusion, maintaining a strained relationship with her husband. She actively learned Russian, cultivated relationships with court officials, and built her own political network. During this period, she secretly studied numerous political texts and corresponded with Enlightenment thinkers like Voltaire. In 1762, after Peter III ascended the throne, she orchestrated a palace coup, overthrowing her husband and proclaiming herself Empress Catherine II.

points.title: 统治巩固
points.description: 即位初期，叶卡捷琳娜面临贵族叛乱和普鲁士入侵的威胁。她通过拉拢贵族阶层，颁布《贵族自由和特权宣言》，巩固了自己的统治地位。她推行了一系列行政改革，完善了地方管理制度，建立了省级行政机构。同时，她开始推行启蒙政策，鼓励教育发展，创办了多家学校和科学院。1767年，她主持召开了立法委员会，试图编纂新法典，虽然最终未能完成，但体现了她试图改革俄国法律体系的努力。
points.descriptionEn: During her early reign, Catherine faced threats from noble rebellions and Prussian invasions. She consolidated her power by allying with the aristocracy and issuing the Manifesto on the Freedom and Privileges of the Nobility. She implemented a series of administrative reforms, improving local governance and establishing provincial administrative structures. Concurrently, she began implementing Enlightenment policies, promoting education by founding numerous schools and academies. In 1767, she convened the Legislative Commission to draft a new legal code, an effort that ultimately remained unfinished but demonstrated her commitment to reforming Russia's legal system.

points.title: 南疆扩张
points.description: 叶卡捷琳娜将目光投向南方，通过两次俄土战争（1768-1774和1787-1792），成功将克里米亚半岛纳入俄国版图，获得了黑海的出海口。她建立了黑海舰队，在克里米亚建立了新城市和海军基地。这一扩张不仅增强了俄国的国际地位，也为俄国提供了温暖的港口和贸易通道。同时，她鼓励德意志人移民到新征服的领土，建立了伏尔加河德意志人殖民地，促进了该地区的经济发展。
points.descriptionEn: Catherine turned her attention southward, through two Russo-Turkish wars (1768-1774 and 1787-1792), successfully incorporating the Crimean Peninsula into Russian territory and gaining access to the Black Sea. She established the Black Sea Fleet and founded new cities and naval bases in Crimea. This expansion not only enhanced Russia's international standing but also provided warm ports and trade routes. Concurrently, she encouraged German immigration to the conquered territories, establishing Volga German colonies and promoting economic development in the region.

points.title: 瓜分波兰
points.description: 叶卡捷琳娜积极参与了三次瓜分波兰（1772, 1793, 1795），极大地扩展了俄国的西部疆域。她支持波兰贵族中的亲俄派，削弱波兰的中央集权，最终导致波兰亡国。这一行动虽然增强了俄国的领土和影响力，但也使叶卡捷琳娜面临欧洲其他国家的批评。同时，她镇压了普加乔夫起义（1773-1775），巩固了国内统治。这一时期，她继续推行文化政策，资助艺术和科学，建立了埃尔米塔日博物馆的雏形。
points.descriptionEn: Catherine actively participated in the three partitions of Poland (1772, 1793, 1795), significantly expanding Russia's western territories. She supported pro-Russian factions among Polish nobility, weakening Poland's central authority and ultimately leading to the country's disappearance. Although this action increased Russia's territory and influence, it also drew criticism from other European powers. Concurrently, she suppressed the Pugachev Rebellion (1773-1775), consolidating domestic rule. During this period, she continued her cultural policies, sponsoring arts and sciences and laying the foundation for the Hermitage Museum.

points.title: 晚年统治
points.description: 叶卡捷琳娜晚年继续推行开明专制政策，但同时也加强了中央集权。她与法国启蒙思想家保持密切联系，但法国大革命爆发后，她转向保守立场，担心革命思想会蔓延到俄国。她建立了秘密警察机构，加强对社会的控制。1796年，叶卡捷琳娜去世，享年67岁，由她的儿子保罗一世继位。她的统治时期被称为叶卡捷琳娜时代，是俄国历史上的黄金时代之一，俄国在政治、军事、文化和教育方面都取得了显著成就。
points.descriptionEn: In her later years, Catherine continued to pursue enlightened absolutism while simultaneously strengthening central authority. She maintained close ties with French Enlightenment thinkers but shifted to a conservative stance after the French Revolution, fearing revolutionary ideas would spread to Russia. She established a secret police agency to increase social control. Catherine died in 1796 at age 67, succeeded by her son Paul I. Her reign, known as the Catherine Era, is considered one of Russia's golden ages, with significant achievements in politics, military affairs, culture, and education.

appraisal.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜大帝通常被视为俄国历史上最重要的统治者之一：她通过领土扩张使俄国跻身欧洲强国，兴办教育与科学机构，赞助艺术，并与伏尔泰等启蒙思想家通信，其统治被称为俄国启蒙的黄金时代。不过也有研究者指出，她一面宣扬启蒙，一面维持专制，镇压普加乔夫起义、设立秘密警察，瓜分波兰，并在宣称改善农奴处境的同时强化并扩大了农奴制。学界因此多把她看作复杂而矛盾的人物：既推动现代化，又维护封建特权，其统治是俄国由传统走向现代的关键过渡。
appraisal.en: Catherine the Great is generally counted among Russia's most consequential rulers: territorial expansion made Russia a European power, she founded educational and scientific institutions, patronized the arts, and corresponded with Enlightenment thinkers such as Voltaire, so that her reign is called a golden age of the Russian Enlightenment. Yet historians also note that she preached Enlightenment while ruling as an autocrat, crushing the Pugachev Rebellion, creating a secret police, partitioning Poland, and strengthening and extending serfdom even as she claimed to improve the serfs' lot. She is therefore widely seen as a complex, contradictory figure who modernized Russia while preserving feudal privilege, her reign a crucial transition from tradition to modernity.

supporter.zh: 叶卡捷琳娜被视为俄罗斯历史上最伟大的统治者之一。她通过领土扩张使俄国成为欧洲强国，推行开明政策促进文化繁荣，建立了完善的教育体系和科学机构。她与伏尔泰等启蒙思想家的通信交流展示了她对知识的追求，而她对艺术的赞助则使俄国文化达到了新的高度。她的统治被称为叶卡捷琳娜时代，是俄罗斯启蒙运动的黄金时期。
supporter.en: Catherine is regarded as one of Russia's greatest rulers. Through territorial expansion, she transformed Russia into a European power, implemented enlightened policies that promoted cultural flourishing, and established comprehensive educational and scientific institutions. Her correspondence with Enlightenment thinkers like Voltaire demonstrated her pursuit of knowledge, while her patronage of the arts elevated Russian culture to new heights. Her reign, known as the Catherine Era, represents a golden age of the Russian Enlightenment.

critic.zh: 批评者指出叶卡捷琳娜的统治存在严重矛盾。她一方面宣扬启蒙思想，另一方面却实行专制统治，镇压普加乔夫起义，建立秘密警察。她对波兰的瓜分被视为背信弃义，而她个人的私生活也备受争议。此外，虽然她宣称改善农奴处境，但实际上却进一步强化了农奴制度，扩大了农奴数量，使数百万俄罗斯人陷入更深的奴役。
critic.en: Critics point to significant contradictions in Catherine's rule. While promoting Enlightenment ideals, she maintained an autocratic regime, suppressing the Pugachev Rebellion and establishing a secret police. Her partition of Poland is viewed as a betrayal of trust, and her personal life was the subject of considerable scandal. Furthermore, despite claiming to improve the serfs' conditions, she actually strengthened the serfdom system, increasing the number of serfs and entrenching millions of Russians in deeper bondage.

objective.zh: 历史学界普遍认为叶卡捷琳娜是一位复杂而矛盾的历史人物。她既是启蒙思想的拥护者，又是专制君主；既推动了俄国的现代化，又维护了封建特权。在流行文化中，她常被描绘为既有政治智慧又有个人魅力的强势女性形象。她的统治代表了俄国从传统向现代过渡的关键时期，其政策影响深远，塑造了俄罗斯帝国的发展轨迹。
objective.en: Historians generally view Catherine as a complex and contradictory figure. She was both an advocate of Enlightenment ideas and an absolute monarch; she promoted Russia's modernization while preserving feudal privileges. In popular culture, she is often depicted as a powerful woman combining political wisdom with personal charisma. Her reign represents a crucial transitional period in Russia's move from tradition to modernity, with policies that profoundly shaped the trajectory of the Russian Empire.

self.zh: 我宁愿我的统治被指责为过于仁慈，而不是过于严厉。
self.en: I would rather my reign be censured for being too lenient than for being too severe.
